questions.question: Describe how the frame of a traditional dome-shaped home is built.
questions.expected_answer: Thin, bendy poles are pushed into the ground in a circle. Their tops are bent over towards the middle and tied together. More poles are tied around in rings, crossing the upright poles, and they are tied wherever they cross, making a strong dome frame.

questions.question: Explain why the Nama matjieshuis suited the life of the Nama people.
questions.expected_answer: The Nama moved with their sheep and goats to find grazing and water. The matjieshuis could be taken apart, with the mats rolled up and the sticks untied, carried on pack animals and put up again. The reed mats kept it cool in hot weather and swelled to keep out rain.

questions.question: What is the job of the frame and what is the job of the covering in an indigenous home?
questions.expected_answer: The frame of struts gives the home its strength and shape and holds it up. The covering, such as reed mats, thatch grass or mud, keeps out the sun, wind, rain and cold.
